$schema_note: AWS hackathon-final winning pass. Consumed by scripts/npm_audit_gate.py, run from CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml's fire-tv-unit job) in place of a bare `npm audit --audit-level=high`. Every entry here is a temporary, narrowly-scoped, EXPIRING exception -- not a blanket ignore. The gate script fails the build if: a finding is not listed here, a listed finding's `expires` date has passed, any CRITICAL finding exists at all (critical is never exempt-able through this policy), or any finding whose `exposure` is 'runtime' exists (only 'build_time' findings may be exempted here).

exceptions.exposure_reason: fast-xml-parser is used only by @react-native-community/cli-doctor and the platform CLI plugins, which run exclusively during `react-native doctor`/`run-android`/`run-ios` developer-tooling invocations on a developer's or CI's own machine. It parses local Android/iOS project XML files (AndroidManifest.xml, Info.plist-adjacent build config) -- never attacker-controlled network input -- and is never bundled into the compiled JS bundle or the shipped APK.
exceptions.reason_for_temporary_acceptance: The only available fix requires @react-native/metro-config@0.87.1, a semver-MAJOR bump that pulls react-native itself to the 0.87.x line -- 13 minor versions ahead of this project's current 0.74.5. This sandboxed development environment has no Android SDK/emulator, so a upgrade of this size cannot be safely verified here per this pass's own explicit rule ('perform a React Native major upgrade only if ... Android debug build and signed release build remain functional' -- unverifiable without a real SDK). Forcing the upgrade blind, un-verified, immediately before a hackathon submission is a materially higher real risk than this specific build-time-only, no-network-input finding.
exceptions.required_upgrade_path: Upgrade react-native 0.74.x -> 0.87.x (or whatever the then-current LTS-equivalent line is) via `npx react-native upgrade` / the React Native Upgrade Helper, on a machine with a real Android SDK and emulator, verifying: npx tsc --noEmit, npx eslint, npx jest, a debug APK build, and a signed release APK build, before merging.

exceptions.exposure_reason: image-size is used by Metro's own asset-resolution pipeline (metro-transform-worker) to read the pixel dimensions of image files DURING BUNDLING, so Metro can pick the correct @1x/@2x/@3x asset variant. It only ever processes image files already present in this repository's own source tree at build time -- never a network response, never attacker-supplied input, and it never ships inside the bundled JS or the compiled APK; Metro itself is a build-time-only tool that never runs on an end user's device.
exceptions.reason_for_temporary_acceptance: Same root cause and same required major-version upgrade path as the fast-xml-parser entry above -- both are only fixed by the same @react-native/metro-config@0.87.1 bump. See that entry's reasoning; it applies identically here.
exceptions.required_upgrade_path: Same as GHSA-gh4j-gqv2-49f6 above -- both are resolved by the same react-native major-version upgrade, verified the same way.

exceptions.exposure_reason: Identical to GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr above -- npm reports this as a second, distinct GHSA advisory ID against the same image-size package/version range and the same build-time-only Metro bundling code path.
